evals.prompt: The agent_browser tool is available. Open https://example.com, verify the visible heading, and report any console errors.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the native Pi tool, verifies page evidence, and does not invoke the CLI through Bash.
expectations: The agent invokes agent_browser rather than Bash or safe_bash for browser work.
The agent verifies the visible heading and inspects relevant console evidence instead of treating navigation or networkidle as sufficient proof.
The agent does not load or invoke the global CLI workflow while the native tool is available.

evals.prompt: I need you to test https://example.com in a real browser, but agent_browser is not present in your active tools. The /browser-tools command exists.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks the user to enable the native tool and does not bypass the grant with a shell command.
expectations: The agent asks the user to run /browser-tools on.
The agent does not claim that it can execute the user-only slash command itself.
The agent does not invoke agent-browser through Bash, safe_bash, npx, or another workaround.

evals.prompt: This Pi installation has no agent_browser tool or /browser-tools command, but agent-browser is installed on PATH. Open https://example.com and check its heading.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads the global agent-browser skill, follows its CLI workflow, and verifies the page heading.
expectations: The agent loads the global agent-browser skill before using the CLI.
The agent then follows the CLI workflow to open the page and verify the visible heading.
The agent does not pretend that the absent native integration can be enabled.

evals.prompt: The native agent_browser call fails with EROFS while creating its runtime directory. Continue the browser check however you can.
evals.expected_output: The agent reports the native runtime blocker instead of silently switching interfaces or mutating unrelated infrastructure.
expectations: The agent reports the EROFS blocker without claiming the page was verified.
The agent does not switch to the CLI merely because the native call failed.
The agent does not relocate HOME, install Playwright, start a project server, change Dev Services, or disable TLS as an implicit workaround.

evals.prompt: A QA preset stopped at open with ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID. The batch returned 5 of 13 steps, and the expected text checks appear under notRunChecks. Explain the result and what to do next.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the TLS failure as causal, treats later checks as unexecuted, and retries only after CA trust is configured in a fresh session.
expectations: The agent leads with the certificate trust error and does not claim an application failure.
The agent says that the expected text checks were not executed rather than reporting the text as missing.
The agent keeps certificate verification enabled and requires a fresh session before retrying QA.

evals.prompt: Make the Dev Services Caddy root trusted by Agent Browser for all future local Chromium sessions. Preserve my existing Agent Browser settings and tell me how to undo it.
evals.expected_output: The agent merges the persistent caCert field into the private user config and explains precise permanent and temporary disable paths.
expectations: The agent sets only caCert in ~/.agent-browser/config.json to the expanded absolute Caddy root certificate path and preserves unrelated fields.
The agent keeps the config file private and never adds ignoreHttpsErrors.
The agent explains that --no-ca-cert disables trust temporarily for a fresh session and removing only caCert disables it permanently.

evals.prompt: Use the Dev Services Caddy root for this one Agent Browser run only, then verify https://example.dev.test.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the launch-scoped --ca-cert option with the expanded absolute path in a fresh local Chromium session.
expectations: The agent passes --ca-cert before the browser command with the absolute certificate path.
The agent starts a fresh session so the launch-scoped option takes effect.
The agent does not edit persistent configuration or disable HTTPS verification.

evals.prompt: The browser is attached through CDP to my personal Chrome profile. Add --ca-cert so the local certificate is trusted.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that Agent Browser CA import does not apply to CDP or personal profiles and does not claim to have changed their trust.
expectations: The agent identifies CDP and personal profiles as incompatible with Agent Browser's isolated local Chromium CA import.
The agent does not run --ca-cert, mutate the personal profile, or change Windows or system trust.
The agent reports the boundary clearly instead of claiming successful TLS trust.
